ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, UBOs and material counterparties against FINTRAC reporting requirements, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated lists, Global Affairs Canada sanctions administered under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Magnitsky). Politically exposed persons (PEPs), including heads of state, ministers, senior judges, military leaders, and their family members/close associates, require enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and senior management approval under PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance. Continuous transaction and sanctions screening is mandated for all bank payment rails (Swift_LC and TT_Wire).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) online system, accessed via Alberta.ca / albertacorporateplanning.com, using the NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) report for Alberta name clearance
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in English, French, or both, with numerals, letters, or typographic characters permitted. The name must be distinctive and not confusingly similar to existing corporate, trade, or partnership names on the Alberta Corporate Registry. For non-Latin script investor names, a romanized (Latin alphabet) transliteration must be provided and reflected in the NUANS search; the legal name on the certificate will be the Latin-script version.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Government or any word implying Crown connection
Medical words implying regulated health profession (e.g., Clinic, Radiology) absent Health Canada or relevant regulator approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may (1) file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of Corporations under the Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of the refusal notice, setting out distinctiveness and disclaimer arguments; (2) commission a fresh NUANS search and amend the proposed name to overcome the confusion objections; and (3) seek judicial review in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta where the Registrar refuses an administrative appeal on erroneous legal grounds. A new filing fee and NUANS report fee apply upon refiling.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for the registered office element of an Alberta business corporation, provided the registered office address is located in Alberta, mail-forwarding is operational, and corporate records are accessible at that address during business hours. However, for ISIC 3250 radiation hardware OEM activity (vapor deposition of amorphous silicon cesium iodide DR detectors) the business requires a physical establishment in Canada to obtain a Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) under the Food and Drugs Act and to pass ISO 13485 / MDSAP audits. A virtual office alone will not satisfy Health Canada licensing, product liability insurer, or commercial bank KYB expectations. At minimum, a leased manufacturing, QA, and warehousing facility in Alberta is required for substantive commercial presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate. Estimated 35-45 percent probability of an unannounced or announced physical on-site inspection within the first 18 months of operation, triggered primarily by Health Canada under the Medical Devices Regulations, ISO 13485 or MDSAP certification audits, municipal business licensing, and Canada Border Services Agency import controls on medical devices. Unannounced corporate registry inspections are rare for non-resident-owned standard business corporations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9; incorporation under s. 6 (Articles of Incorporation), registered office under s. 20, directors under s. 101 and s. 106, officers under s. 123
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (also the federal Companies Directorate may apply if federal charter is selected; this dossier assumes provincial incorporation in Alberta)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1200, 'Articles of Incorporation' filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the ABCA; share capital may be nominal and no escrow or capital deposit is required before incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Corporation subscribe for and accept, and that shares be allotted and issued to the subscribers, in accordance with the Articles and any Subscription Agreements. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Corporation shall be located at the address set forth in the Registered Office Form and that the specified authorized representative be designated to act as registered agent for the Corporation. RESOLVED that the following individuals be and each is hereby appointed as officers of the Corporation with the titles and duties set forth in the bylaws: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, each to serve until replaced by a subsequent resolution of the Board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Search and NUANS Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (or an incorporated service provider authorized by the Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name request through the Alberta Corporate Registry's online portal, obtain a NUANS search report, and verify no conflicting existing trade-mark or corporate name exists in Alberta. If a distinctive name is not essential, a numbered company may be immediately incorporated.
required_dossiers: Certificate of name approval or request waiver
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, resubmit with a revised name or proceed with a numbered corporation by filing Articles using the assigned incorporation number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing Articles of Incorporation and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and notarize Articles of Incorporation, execute the authorization for share structure and director information, and submit the filing through the online Corporate Registry system. Pay the prescribed filing fee and retain the stamped or digital receipt. Upon approval, the Registry issues a Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: NUANS report if using a name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried or rejected for incomplete notices, file an amendment or supplementary Form by accessing the same registry dossier, correct the deficiency, and pay any amendment fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Designation and Corporate Records Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Elect a physical registered office address in Alberta, complete the Registered Office Form, and execute the registered office consent. Immediately after incorporation, prepare the corporate minute book, register the registered office in the Company's records, and maintain copies of the Certificate of Incorporation and Articles.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office is rejected for being a postal box without physical premises, provide a street address and re-file the Form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting: Share Subscriptions, Officer Appointments, and Initial Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting (or use unanimous written resolution), adopt the pro-forma board resolution, allot shares to subscribers, receive share subscription funds, appoint officers, adopt bylaws, set fiscal year-end, and open a corporate bank account with documentary evidence for KYC/AML review.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution (as set out in the framework)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer becomes disqualified during the meeting, the Board may by written resolution fill the vacancy immediately and ratify all earlier actions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Alberta Corporate Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); Alberta Corporate Tax and program registration through the CRA's business registration service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a federal Business Number (BN) through the CRA portal, register for the Corporation's income tax account (RC196), GST/HST account (if threshold met), payroll deductions account, and import/export program (if applicable), and activate the Alberta corporate tax registration through the CRA's one-window business registration.
required_dossiers: Estimated annual remuneration or GST/HST filing election
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN is delayed, use the CRA's interim 'Confirmation of Registration' and correct any data validation issues using the CRA's 'My Business Account' portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Licensing and Trade Registry Completions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry; Service Alberta; municipal licensing authority (where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify any provincial or municipal licenses required for the physical manufacturing site, complete any additional sector-specific registrations (e.g., Alberta Labour and Immigration workplace safety), and file the annual return with the Alberta Corporate Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a municipal license is denied due to zoning or occupancy concerns, seek a municipal development permit or conditional use approval and file an appeal to the Subdivision and Development Appeal Board.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Labour and Immigration - Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) and Alberta Municipal Affairs for municipal development permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Alberta Manufacturing / Development Operating Permit (issued by the local municipality under the Municipal Government Act, RSA 2000, c M-26; where hazardous materials are present, an OHS workplace clearance is also required)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (External Environment and Protected Areas division)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (not a full EIA Report) for the manufacture of electronic equipment under the Activities Designation Regulation, A.R. 276/2003, unless the facility meets or exceeds thresholds triggering an Environmental Impact Assessment under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives for volatile organic compounds (VOCs); wastewater discharges to municipal sewer must meet municipal sewer-use bylaws and Alberta's 'Code of Practice' requirements for any industrial effluent; waste handling must conform to the Hazardous Waste Regulation, A.R. 347/1993 for any spent photoconductor or chemical residues

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local municipal fire department, structural load inspection of the manufacturing floor and shielding walls, and an OHS workplace clearance verifying compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Code (Alberta) including radiation protection, electrical safety, and emergency response protocols

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - GST/HST and corporate income tax administration; provincial corporate income tax for Alberta is also collected by the CRA under a tax collection agreement; Alberta Corporate Registry for extra-provincial corporate registration; CBSA for customs and export declaration processing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity carrying on business in Canada must: (1) obtain a federal Business Number (BN) from the CRA by filing Form RC1 or applying online through the 'My Business Account' portal; (2) register for GST/HST if worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a calendar quarter or if the entity voluntarily registers; (3) if operating in Alberta through a physical presence or permanent establishment, complete extra-provincial registration under the Alberta Business Corporations Act and obtain an Alberta Corporate Access Number; (4) where importing or exporting goods, open a CBSA import/export account (linked to the BN) and obtain a Canadian customs client identifier; (5) for non-resident corporate status, submit relevant treaty/withholding documentation to the CRA if a waiver of Part XIII withholding is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not permit a U.S.-style check-the-box election; legal form determines tax classification. A Canadian business corporation is a separate taxpayer subject to federal and provincial income tax. Available statutory elections include: (i) GST/HST joint election under ETA s. 273 to treat related corporations as a single registrant; (ii) ETA s. 156 election for closely related persons to have taxable supplies at nil consideration; (iii) S. 216 election for non-residents with Canadian employment income reporting; and hybrid mismatch rules under ITA ss. 18.4 and 18.5 apply to recharacterize certain cross-border arrangements, but no elective hybrid classification is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax); Alberta applies only the 5% federal GST because the province has no provincial sales tax or HST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in total worldwide taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated exports?) measured over any calendar quarter; once exceeded, GST/HST registration is mandatory. Small suppliers are exempt from mandatory registration until the threshold is breached. Voluntary registration is available for businesses making zero-rated exports to claim input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory government real-time invoice clearance or digital stamping regime at the federal level. GST/HST registrants must issue invoices containing prescribed information (ETA s. 3, Sch. V? actually s. 223 and Regulations). Electronic invoicing is permitted; records must be retained and accessible electronically for CRA inspection. For exports, the CBSA requires electronic pre-export reporting via the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) under the CBSA Assessment and Revenue Management (CARM) platform, with export declarations transmitted through the Canadian Customs Commercial System.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods exported by the supplier to a non-resident person are zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act (ETA) if the supplier has evidence of export within the prescribed time frame (generally 60 days). Services supplied to a non-resident are zero-rated where the service is acquired for use mainly outside Canada and is not performed in Canada to a substantial extent (or is performed only for a non-resident). For medical device components such as amorphous silicon cesium iodide flat panel detectors, zero-rating applies only where the goods are exported as part of a commercial activity and are not excluded by Schedule VI Part IV (some medical devices may be exempt when supplied domestically, but exports are generally zero-rated).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Export Declaration (via CBSA CERS or authorized service provider)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export
Cargo control and customs clearance records
Proof of payment (SWIFT MT103, letter of credit, telegraphic transfer advice) and inward remittance record where applicable
CRA Form GST11 or GST189 for refund applications (where input tax credits exceed liabilities), and internal audit trail of the zero-rating election
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess to disallow zero-rating where export documentation is insufficient or the export does not occur within the required period, resulting in uncollected GST/HST liability, interest, and penalties. Under ETA s. 280, failure to collect or remit can attract penalties up to 15% of the amount; under s. 285, false statements or omissions may incur penalties equal to 10% of the net tax (or greater for knowingly fraudulent filings). Willful evasion can lead to fines of up to 200% of the evaded amount (under s. 327, a fine up to CAD 10,000 per count for summary conviction or CAD 50,000 per count for indictable? actual statutory max? To be safe: significant fines) and imprisonment. Retrospective clawback periods can extend up to 4 years for ordinary reassessments, or beyond 4 years where misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud is shown.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); prudential supervision of deposit-taking institutions by Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); no dedicated foreign-exchange-control authority due to Canada's liberal exchange-control regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act. There is no exchange-control approval for profit remittances, dividends, or cross-border capital movements. Repatriation of earnings is free in CAD or any permitted foreign currency, subject only to corporate-law solvency tests, AML/KYC verification, and Part XIII Canadian non-resident withholding tax (typically reduced by tax treaty).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender or conversion ratios. No mandatory timeline or conversion obligation applies to export receipts; proceeds may be retained in CAD or any foreign currency. Export documentation (customs declarations, commercial invoices, bills of lading) must however be retained, and Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) requires accurate trade records for duty and tax verification.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Low-to-Medium. Offshore digital EMI entities are not permitted to take deposits or hold CAD clearing accounts as deposit institutions under the Bank Act. They may operate in Canada only as registered payment service providers under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) or applicable provincial money-services licensing, with FINTRAC AML obligations. Such accounts can support settlement flows but cannot serve as statutory capital escrow or payroll accounts for an Alberta-incorporated business corporation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Banks require either physical presence or a video-identified KYC interview for directors with 25% or greater ownership and for all account signatories. Remote opening is generally permissible for a Canadian business corporation if the bank uses verified video identification and at least one final approver is physically in Canada. Alberta-based banks also expect one authorised director or a registered Alberta agent to accept regulatory mail and provide a local business address; where a foreign parent controls the entity, a Canadian-resident director or officer is strongly recommended.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners with opaque multi-tier corporate structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry extract, complete beneficial-ownership chart, trust deed or foundation declaration, source-of-wealth statement, and audited financial statements of the ultimate parent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border transactions involving high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanction-screening reports, export control permits from Global Affairs Canada, customs export declarations, commercial invoices, bills of lading, and trade finance documentation evidencing underlying hardware supply.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wire volumes or counterparties inconsistent with an OEM radiology hardware business
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master supply agreements, purchase orders, customs broker statements, warehouse receipts, logistics manifests, and Health Canada radiation-emitting-device registration certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection coded as general remittance without clear equity documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement, unanimous shareholder declaration, board resolutions, Notice of Assessment, and a Canadian tax lawyer opinion confirming the capital nature of the inflow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction frequency immediately post-onboarding before commercial contract evidence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Forward sales contracts, letters of intent, industry association membership, distributor agreements, and director identification with a verified Canadian professional reference.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity capital and shareholder loans must be routed by SWIFT MT103/202 to the Alberta operational or escrow account with a clear purpose code corresponding to 'equity investment' or 'intercompany financing'. Canadian banks require an executed investment resolution and a legal breakdown distinguishing paid-in capital from loan principal; foreign-currency wires are converted to CAD at account value date. Regulatory verifications include FINTRAC reporting for transfers above CAD 10,000, bank's pre-transaction KYC for transfers above CAD 50,000, and OSFI prudential thresholds for large-value settlement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 (telegraphic transfer) for high-value supplier payments, commercial documentary letters of credit under SWIFT MT700 / UCP600 for purchase-order-backed imports, and Payments Canada's CAD-system (CDCS) for domestic clearing. For export of digital X-ray flat panels, each outgoing wire must carry product description under HS 9018 or HS 9022, the underlying commercial invoice, and, where Letters of Credit are used, a full set of clean-on-board transport documents. Health Canada registration for ionizing radiation devices must accompany any shipment to non-Canadian end customers, and GST/HST or zero-rating documentation must be retained for cash-flow recovery.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP, CAD/JPY) executed with a Canadian Schedule I bank
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or lightly traded currencies (e.g., offshore RMB CNH, INR, BRL) with offshore settlement
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term intercompany financing
Plain-vanilla European FX options procured from a regulated Canadian derivatives dealer
Exchange-traded FX futures on CME or ICE for margin-efficient short-term hedging

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation or amalgamation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 100 late-filing charge after the 60-day window; failure to file for three consecutive years permits the Registrar to strike the corporation off the Alberta corporate register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal CBCA Annual Return (applicable if the entity is a federally incorporated business corporation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fee CAD 12 electronic / CAD 20 paper; failure to file for two consecutive years allows the Director to issue a notice of intended dissolution, and if uncured within 120 days, the corporation is dissolved.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return including Alberta Corporate Income Tax schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of each taxation year (fiscal year-end); instalments as required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; 10% base penalty for repeat failures; a parallel Alberta provincial penalty applies to the provincial balance; daily compound interest accrues.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined general corporate rate (15% federal Part I general rate + 8% Alberta provincial rate); a foreign-controlled subsidiary is not a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) and therefore cannot access the federal small business deduction.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal SR&ED investment tax credit (15% non-refundable for non-CCPC; 35% refundable for CCPC on qualifying expenditures up to CAD 3 million) plus Alberta SR&ED tax credit (10% non-refundable for non-CCPC); accelerated CCA under Class 53 for manufacturing and processing equipment; immediate full expensing of qualifying M&P property acquired before 2028; no Alberta capital tax; foreign tax credit relief for foreign-source income.
